newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Oct NZ electricity prices revised lower - EMCO.
newsitem.headline: Oct NZ electricity prices revised lower - EMCO.

text.p: A recalculation of New Zealand average October electricity prices with revised metering data has produced a general reduction in prices, market operator EMCO said on Tuesday.

"On average prices for the North Island (at the Haywards reference point) were 11 percent lower and in the South Island (at the Benmore reference point) three percent lower than the earlier published October prices," EMCO said in a statement.
"This confirms our expectation that the recalculated final prices would be lower than the prices released on November 12."

The average price in the North Island was 3.90 NZ cents a kilowatt hour compared with 4.39 cents in the earlier prices. The highest price was now 15.52 cents a kilowatt hour compared to 33.34 cents earlier.
In the South Isalnd, the average price was 3.12 cents a kilowatt hour compared to 3.21 cents previously. The highest price was now 11.93 cents a kilowatt hour versus 16.18 cents previously.

The electricity market's independent watchdog, the Market Surveillance Committee, ordered the October prices be recalculated after the discovery of errors in the metering data. The committee was continuing its investigation into "ramp rate" violations.
EMCO said the recalculation had removed about half of the earlier price "spikes" which had previously inflated the average prices for the month.
"For example, the 85 price spikes previously in the Haywards prices were reduced to 43. However, others remain -- particularly for three days during the middle of the month," EMCO said.
Final prices for November are due to be published on or before December 11.
